mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between GDPC1 YoY < -2% and subsequent 60-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) rise above 6% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly lower (p > 0.10) when UNRATE first exceeds 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for two consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative relationship (p > 0.05) between INDPRO double-dip and subsequent 20-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a dual labor market shock, amplifying recession risk and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS falls in the same month
failure_condition: No significant increase (p > 0.05) in probability of negative 20-day S&P 500 returns when both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average, sustained for four consecutive months, signals weakening housing demand and negative implications for construction and home-related equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.10) between HOUST < 12-month MA for 4 months and subsequent 60-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) over two consecutive months signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls in two consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant increase (p > 0.05) in probability of negative 20-day S&P 500 returns when both FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 5-year average, combined with a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), signals constrained household balance sheets and reduced consumption capacity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 5-year average AND GDPC1 YoY decline
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between the joint trigger and subsequent 60-day S&P 500 returns.
